newsitem.title: MEXICO: Accused Mexican drug lord had vast empire - report.
newsitem.headline: Accused Mexican drug lord had vast empire - report.

text.p: Alleged Mexican drug kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego controlled a vast legal and illegal business empire on both sides of the U.S.-Mexican border before his arrest early this year, a Mexican newspaper reported on Sunday.

Garcia Abrego ran hotels, real estate and an air taxi service in south Texas and held billions of dollars in bank accounts and investments, El Financiero reported, citing a 50-page Mexican Attorney General's Office report.
Garcia Abrego, who allegedly controlled the Gulf cartel moving enormous quantities of cocaine across the border, is currently on trial in U.S. federal court in Houston.
He was arrested in Mexico and extradited to the United States for trial on the basis of a U.S. passport he possessed.
El Financiero, a Mexico City daily, said details from the Mexican report may surface in Garcia Abrego's U.S. trial.
In the south Texas border cities of Brownsville and Laredo, Garcia Abrego ran gambling halls, air taxi services, hotels and real estate, the report said.
The air taxi business routinely altered flight logs for planes carrying drugs, the report said.

South of the border, his business holdings were even more extensive, including newspapers, hotels, construction firms, lumber companies, moving businesses, ranches, real estate and clandestine airstrips, the report said.

"The air strips are of particular interest (to authorities) because together with a money laundering network they could lead to important politicians and business people, both national and foreign," El Financiero said.
According to unconfirmed media reports in Mexico, Garcia Abrego had links to Raul Salinas de Gortari, the brother of former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari.
Raul Salinas is in jail on murder and corruption charges. Investigators have discovered up to $300 million he had stashed in secret European bank accounts.
Carlos Salinas fled Mexico in disgrace and lives in exile in Ireland.
According to the El Financiero report, Garcia Abrego was so powerful he easily was able to corrupt Mexican state and federal judges as well as the Mexican Navy by delivering envelopes full of cash.
